title: My Vibe Coded Game
author: HallucinatedGames
selftext:
Here is how I built this vibe coded game - Kaiju Havoc — a browser-based Tokyo destruction simulator where you play as a giant monster stomping buildings, fighting the military, and racking up combos.

  I'd describe what I wanted in plain English to Claude Code, and it would write the JavaScript, set up the Three.js scene graph, wire up the game loop, build the enemy AI, etc. The whole thing was iterative — I'd play it, say "the buildings are too tanky" or "the strafe is reversed" or "add destructible bridges over the river," and Claude would make the changes. The git log reads like a director's commentary.

For 3D models, I used Meshy AI to generate GLB files — all three playable kaiju with 18-21 animation clips each, 24+ unique buildings (Tokyo Tower, Skytree, temples, skyscrapers), debris chunks, vehicles, trees, even the bridges. The game preloads all templates during a loading screen then clones them per-instance.

The full code and prompt history for anyone to follow is here: [corycowgill/Kaiju](https://github.com/corycowgill/Kaiju)
